skill.name: allaymc-plugin-dev
skill.description: Create, update, and troubleshoot AllayMC plugins for Minecraft Bedrock servers using Java or other JVM languages.
skill.summary: Guides AllayMC plugin setup, metadata, lifecycle code, builds, and troubleshooting.
skill.author: AllayMC

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by LGPL text and Markdown inline code in SKILL.md and README.md. Two findings are confirmed because the skill directs agents to run project-local Gradle wrapper tasks, which can execute workspace build logic. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to inspect Gradle wrapper files and build scripts, then ask the user before running runServer or shadowJar.
Document that build commands should only run in user-approved workspaces and should use the existing project directory.

remediation.issue: Scanner noise from inline code spans
remediation.suggestion: Separate non-executable identifiers from runnable command guidance so automated review can distinguish terms from commands.

content.value_statement: AllayMC plugin authors need accurate API guidance and setup steps. This skill guides project setup, lifecycle code, Gradle metadata, local builds, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Guides new AllayMC plugin setup from the Java plugin template.
Updates Gradle metadata, package names, authors, website, and API version settings.
Creates plugin entry classes with AllayMC lifecycle methods.
Uses local AllayMC documentation and source references for API guidance.
Explains local build and run tasks for AllayGradle projects.
Highlights threading and nullability considerations for plugin code.
limitations: Requires an existing workspace or template files for project edits.
Build and run steps depend on the local Gradle wrapper and project configuration.
API guidance depends on the bundled AllayMC reference sources being current.
Does not replace testing on a real Minecraft Bedrock server environment.

use_cases.title: Start a New Plugin
use_cases.description: Create an AllayMC plugin project with metadata, package names, and an entry class.

use_cases.title: Migrate Existing Plugin Code
use_cases.description: Adapt a Java plugin structure to AllayMC APIs, lifecycle methods, and Gradle settings.

use_cases.title: Debug Build Problems
use_cases.description: Review AllayGradle configuration, plugin metadata, and API usage when a plugin fails to build or load.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to create a new AllayMC plugin named WelcomeTools. Ask me for any required metadata before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Plugin Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to update my plugin package, authors, website, API version, and plugin entry class. Explain each file change.

prompt_templates.title: Add Plugin Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to add the lifecycle logic for my AllayMC plugin. Check the bundled API references before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Loading Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to diagnose why my AllayMC plugin does not load. Inspect metadata, Gradle settings, lifecycle methods, and logs.

output_examples.input: Create a new AllayMC plugin for welcome messages.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for plugin metadata, prepares the project structure, describes the entry class, and lists build steps for review.

output_examples.input: My plugin builds but does not load on the server.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks metadata, entry class naming, API version settings, and lifecycle methods, then gives a focused fix list.

output_examples.input: Migrate this plugin to AllayMC APIs.
output_examples.output: The assistant compares the existing structure with AllayMC expectations and recommends package, lifecycle, and Gradle changes.

best_practices: Provide plugin name, package name, authors, website, and target Allay API version before setup.
Review Gradle wrapper and build files before approving local build or run tasks.
Test lifecycle behavior and thread-sensitive code in a local server environment.
anti_patterns: Running Gradle tasks in an untrusted workspace without user approval.
Changing package names without updating the plugin entrance setting.
Ignoring AllayMC threading behavior when adding event or lifecycle logic.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build, update, and troubleshoot AllayMC plugins for Minecraft Bedrock servers.

faq.question: Which languages does it support?
faq.answer: It focuses on Java and other JVM languages used with AllayMC and Gradle.

faq.question: Does it include AllayMC references?
faq.answer: Yes. It points the agent to bundled AllayMC docs, source references, AllayGradle, and a Java plugin template.

faq.question: Can it run the plugin locally?
faq.answer: It can suggest local Gradle run steps, but users should approve command execution first.

faq.question: Is it only for new projects?
faq.answer: No. It can also help migrate existing plugins and troubleshoot build or loading failures.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the plugin name, package name, authors, website, target Allay API version, and desired behavior.
